claims.text: The initial Fe-Co-Ni-Ti alloy is a metastable single-phase fcc high-entropy alloy with Ti dissolved in the fcc lattice.
The initial alloy has a suppressed orbital moment and coercivity below 50 Oe.
Controlled annealing can precipitate a Ti-rich L21-ordered Heusler phase, such as Fe2TiNi, while retaining the fcc Fe-Co-Ni-Ti matrix.
Maintaining 10–20 vol% L21 precipitates will avoid single-phase L21 behavior.
The fcc matrix and L21 phase will remain structurally and magnetically stable between approximately 300 K and 600 K.
The L21 precipitates will form coherent interfaces with the fcc matrix.
Precipitate–matrix coherence and lattice misfit will generate local lattice strain.
The coherent interfaces will modify the electronic density of states and enhance the orbital magnetic moment.
The L21 phase has a distinct magnetic ground state and higher orbital angular momentum than the disordered fcc phase.
The fcc/L21 interfaces act as domain-wall pinning centers.
Chemical ordering in the L21 phase prevents orbital-moment quenching and thereby increases magnetic anisotropy and coercivity.
Introducing 10–20 vol% coherent L21 phase will raise coercivity above 100 Oe at room and elevated temperatures.
Coercivity will increase with L21 volume fraction up to approximately 20 vol%.
Above approximately 20 vol% L21, brittleness or precipitate coarsening may cause a loss of coercivity.
The single-phase fcc baseline has low coercivity because it lacks domain-wall pinning sites and has a suppressed orbital moment.
Decomposition of the L21 phase into B2/BCC structures would eliminate the required magnetic coupling.
Current thermodynamic databases do not accurately establish L21 stability in the specific Fe-Co-Ni-Ti system.
The relationship between L21 ordering and orbital-moment enhancement in this fcc Fe-Co-Ni-Ti matrix is not yet quantitatively established.
Rapid quenching will produce a single-phase fcc control, whereas controlled annealing will produce an otherwise comparable alloy containing 15 vol% L21.
A failure of the dual-phase material to exceed 100 Oe and increase its orbital-to-spin moment ratio relative to the single-phase control would falsify the proposed mechanism.
